routes.name: Visa-free short stay (Schengen, up to 90 days in 180)
routes.summary: Citizens of countries on Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806 (for example the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, Brazil) can visit Spain without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. You still need to show your purpose, enough money and a valid passport.

other: Your country must be on the official visa-exempt list (Annex II). Some exemptions only apply to biometric passports.
Passport valid at least 3 months after you leave the Schengen area and issued within the last 10 years.
Border officers can ask for a return ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of money (2026 minimum is EUR 122 per day, or EUR 1,099 for stays of 9 days or more).
Days count across the whole Schengen area, not just Spain. No work allowed.

sources.label: Spain Consulate in Washington: Conditions for entry into Spain
Spain Consulate in Washington: Schengen visa-required and visa-exempt list

routes.name: ETIAS travel authorization (not live yet)
routes.summary: Visa-exempt visitors will need an ETIAS travel authorization before flying to Spain once the EU system starts. Spain's consulate page says it is expected to start in the last quarter of 2026. Check the EU site for the real start date.

other: Applies to visa-exempt nationalities only.
Not required yet as of the date checked. The start date will be announced several months ahead.
Fee and validity were not stated on the Spanish page.

sources.label: Spain Consulate in Washington: Conditions for entry into Spain (ETIAS section)

routes.name: Short-stay Schengen visa (tourism, business, family visits)
routes.summary: If your country is not visa-exempt, you apply for a short-stay Schengen visa at a Spanish consulate. It covers stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period for tourism, business, family visits, medical treatment or short study.

other: Applies to nationalities on the visa-required list (Annex I of EU Regulation 2018/1806).
Travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000 for the whole stay.
Proof of money: EUR 122 per day for trips under 9 days, EUR 1,099 for trips of 9 days or more (2026 figures).
Passport valid at least 90 days past departure, issued within the last 10 years.
Apply 6 months to 15 days before travel.

documents: Proof of funds and employment or enrollment
Proof of legal residence if you apply outside your home country

fees.label: Standard fee at the Washington consulate, ages 12 and over (2026)
fees.note: Varies by consulate and nationality. Revised quarterly.

routes.processing: Legal decision period is 15 calendar days, up to 45 days if an interview or more documents are requested.

sources.label: Spain Consulate in Washington: Schengen visas
Spain Consulate in Washington: Schengen visa-required and visa-exempt list

routes.name: Transit through Spain and Spanish airports
routes.summary: A Schengen visa lets you pass through Spanish territory and airports. The Spanish consular page does not list which nationalities need a separate airport transit visa, so check the official Schengen rules before you book a layover.

other: Airside transit visa rules and the list of nationalities that need one were not found on the pages we could open.
If you are visa-exempt for Schengen, you can transit like any other short stay.

sources.label: Spain Consulate in Washington: Schengen visas

routes.name: Telework (Digital Nomad) Visa and Residence Permit
routes.summary: For remote workers and freelancers who work for companies outside Spain. You can apply at a consulate or, if you are already legally in Spain, for the residence permit directly. The permit can last up to three years.

income.note: 200% of the minimum wage (SMI) as stated in a July 2025 embassy document. The SMI has changed since, so confirm the current figure.

eligibility.education: Relevant degree, or at least 3 years of equivalent professional experience
other: Work must be remote for companies based outside Spain.
Employees can only work for non-Spanish companies. Self-employed people can also serve Spanish clients, up to 20% of their activity.
Proof of at least 3 months of relationship with the foreign company or clients, and the company must have operated at least one year.
Health insurance valid in Spain, no waiting periods or co-pay gaps. Travel insurance is not accepted.
Clean criminal record.
Family members need extra income: 75% of the minimum wage for the first family member, 25% for each additional one.

stay.note: The visa is valid up to 1 year. The residence permit can be valid for a maximum of three years. Renewal and permanent residence rules were not stated on the pages we could open.

steps: Gather documents and book an in-person consular appointment (online applications are not accepted).
Apply for the visa and NIE together.
Collect the visa within 1 month of approval.
Enter Spain and register with Social Security as required.
documents: Passport valid at least 1 year, with two blank pages
Certificate from the foreign company or client, dated at least 3 months before applying
Company registry certificate showing at least one year of operations
Degree or proof of 3 years of experience
Family documents if applying with relatives
routes.processing: Legal decision period is 10 days from the day after submission. Can be longer if an interview or more documents are requested.

sources.label: Spain Embassy in Ottawa: Telework visa (Digital Nomad)
Spain Embassy in Nicosia: Digital Nomad Visa requirements (PDF)

routes.name: Non-Lucrative Residence (retirement and passive income)
routes.summary: Live in Spain on savings or passive income without working. The first permit lasts one year, then renews in two-year periods. You cannot work, including remotely.

income.note: 400% of IPREM (IPREM is EUR 600 per month, so EUR 2,400 per month). Add 100% of IPREM (EUR 7,200 per year) per family member. Figure from the Washington consulate page, 2026.

other: No work or professional activity in Spain, including remote work.
Public or private health insurance with an insurer authorized in Spain, with full coverage and no co-pay.
Medical certificate and clean criminal record from every country lived in during the last 5 years.
Passport valid at least 1 year.
For renewal you must live in Spain more than 183 days per calendar year.

stay.note: Renewals are for 2 years. The consular visa itself is short, so enter Spain within its validity.

steps: Apply for the national visa at the Spanish consulate for your area, with form EX-01.
After approval, collect the visa and enter Spain.
Apply in person for the foreigner identity card (TIE) within 1 month of arrival.
documents: Proof of funds (bank statements, certificates, income documents)
Criminal record certificate with apostille and sworn translation

fees.label: Visa fee for US citizens at the Washington consulate (2026)

routes.processing: The legal decision period is 3 months, and can be longer. Consultations with other authorities can take up to 3 more months.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 6, initial non-lucrative residence
Ministry of Inclusion: renewal of non-lucrative residence
Spain Consulate in Washington: Non-lucrative residence visa

routes.name: Residence and Work Authorization for Employees
routes.summary: A Spanish employer applies for your permit. The job must be on the hard-to-fill occupations list, or the employer must show the vacancy could not be filled locally. The permit is tied to the employer.

other: Signed contract guaranteeing continuous work during the permit. Pay at least the minimum wage (SMI), pro-rated for part time.
Occupation on the SEPE quarterly hard-to-fill list, or the employer proves no local worker could fill it.
Training and any legally required professional qualification for the job.
Employer is registered with Social Security and up to date on taxes.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years. Not already in Spain irregularly.
Exceptions to the labor market test exist for nationals of Chile and Peru under international agreements.

stay.note: More than 90 days and less than 5 years. Renewal rules are on a separate Ministry sheet.

steps: Employer files the application electronically (Mercurio portal) or in person at the government delegation.
After approval, you request the visa at the Spanish consulate in your country.
Enter Spain, register with Social Security and apply for your foreigner identity card.
routes.processing: Decision due within 3 months of registration. Silence is treated as a refusal.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Initial residence and work authorization for employees

routes.name: Highly Qualified Professional and EU Blue Card
routes.summary: Fast-track residence and work permit for degree holders or experienced professionals with a job offer. There are two flavors: a national permit and the EU Blue Card. Permits last up to three years.

eligibility.education: Blue Card: higher education of at least 3 years (EQF level 6), or 5 years of relevant experience. National permit: lower degree level or 3 years of equivalent experience.
other: Blue Card needs a contract or firm offer of at least 6 months.
A lower salary threshold (80%) applies in some cases, such as recent graduates. The exact salary figure was not stated on the page.
Health insurance and enough resources for you and your family.
No criminal record in Spain or the last 2 countries of residence.

stay.note: Up to 3 years, or contract length plus 3 months if shorter.

routes.processing: Decision in 20 days from electronic submission. If there is no answer, it is deemed granted. Then the consulate decides the visa within 10 working days.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 66, highly qualified professionals

routes.name: Residence and Self-Employment Authorization (freelancers and entrepreneurs)
routes.summary: For people who want to start a business or freelance in Spain. You need to show the investment is enough, the business meets legal requirements, and you hold the needed qualifications. The first permit lasts one year and is limited to a region and sector.

other: No minimum investment amount is set. You prove the investment is sufficient and show its effect on jobs. A valuation report from bodies such as ATA, UPTA or CIAE can be used.
Licenses or permits needed to open the activity, with their status.
Required professional qualification or accredited experience, with recognition of foreign degrees where needed.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.

stay.note: Limited to a region and sector at first. Renewal has its own Ministry sheet.

routes.processing: Decision within 3 months. Then request the visa within 1 month and enter Spain within its 3-month validity. Register with Social Security within 3 months of entry.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Initial residence and self-employment authorization

routes.name: Seasonal Work Authorization
routes.summary: For seasonal jobs such as farm work. You can work up to nine months in a calendar year. The authorization lasts four years and is tied to one employer, with a fixed-discontinuous contract.

other: You must be outside Spain when applying and commit to return home after the season.
Employer proves the labor market need, pays travel costs, and provides housing and health insurance until Social Security registration.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.

stay.note: Work is limited to 9 months per calendar year.

steps: Employer files form EX-06 electronically at least 2 months before work starts.
You apply for the visa at a Spanish consulate within 1 month of notification.
Enter Spain and register with Social Security via the employer. Apply for your identity card within 1 month.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet on seasonal residence and work

routes.name: Residence and Work for Researchers
routes.summary: For researchers, university professors and enrolled doctoral students hosted by a Spanish research entity. The first permit lasts three years and family members can join.

other: A hosting entity or employment contract with defined research content and dates.
Health insurance and enough resources for you and your family.
No criminal record in Spain or the last 2 countries of residence.

stay.note: Initial 3 years, renewals of 2 years. After research ends you can stay up to 12 months to look for related work or start a business.

routes.processing: Decision in 20 working days. If there is no answer, it is deemed granted.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 68, researchers

routes.name: Student Stay (higher education and secondary)
routes.summary: Long-stay permit for full-time study at a recognized Spanish institution. It lasts as long as the course for higher education. Family members can come but cannot work.

other: Income rule: The rule is 100% of IPREM per month (50% if housing is prepaid for the whole stay). The page gives percentages only. IPREM is EUR 600 per month per another official page.
Admission to a recognized institution with fees paid.
Health insurance from an insurer authorized in Spain.
Medical certificate and criminal record certificate for stays over 6 months (adults).
Apply at least 2 months before classes start where possible.
Family members: 75% of IPREM for the first, 50% for each extra.

stay.note: Equal to the length of the studies for higher education. Secondary education is capped at 1 year. Up to two extensions.

routes.processing: From abroad, decision within 1 month at the consulate. Silence means refusal.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Study stays
Ministry of Inclusion: Reglamento de Extranjería overview (students can work up to 30 hours a week)

routes.name: Post-Study Job Search or Business Start Permit
routes.summary: After finishing a university-level degree (EQF level 6 or higher) in Spain, you can apply for a 24-month permit to look for a job or start a business. It cannot be extended.

eligibility.education: Completed studies at a Spanish higher education institution, at least EQF level 6
other: Income rule: 100% of IPREM per month (50% if housing is prepaid). The page gives percentages only.
You must hold a study stay (or its extension) when applying.
Apply within 60 days before your study permit expires.
Health insurance and no criminal record.

The page says holders are not authorized to work on this permit and must apply for a work or self-employment authorization for a suitable job. Check this wording, since the regulation press release describes a job-search permit extended to one year.

routes.processing: Decision due within 20 days. Silence may be treated as approval.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 20, job search or business start

routes.name: Working Holiday and Youth Mobility Visa
routes.summary: Young people from partner countries can live in Spain for a limited time with tourism as the main purpose and some work. Spain has youth mobility agreements with Argentina, South Korea, Japan, Australia, Canada and New Zealand.

other: Terms differ by country. For Australians: age 18 to 30, at least AUD 1,026 per month in funds, at least 2 years of higher education, basic Spanish, no dependants, and no more than 6 months with one employer.
Check the consulate page for your country for age limits, length and fees.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Youth mobility agreements
Spain Consulate in Melbourne: Working Holiday visa

routes.name: Family Reunification (for relatives of foreign residents)
routes.summary: A foreign resident who has lived in Spain at least one year and has renewed for at least another year can bring a spouse or partner, children, dependent relatives and some parents. Spouses and working-age children can work.

other: Income rule: The rule is 150% of IPREM per month for a two-person unit, plus 50% for each extra member. The page gives percentages only. IPREM is EUR 600 per month per another official page.
Sponsor has lived in Spain at least 1 year and applied to renew for at least another year (exceptions for long-term residents).
Adequate housing, health insurance and stable resources.
Spouse or partner must be over 18 and only one partner can be reunited. Stable partners need 12 months living together unless they have children.
Parents must be over 65 and in your care, with some humanitarian exceptions.

stay.note: Valid until the sponsor's permit ends, minimum 1 year.

routes.processing: Decision in 2 months. After approval the relative has 2 months to apply for the visa.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Family reunification

routes.name: Residence for Relatives of Spanish Nationals
routes.summary: Spouses, partners, children under 26, parents and certain other relatives of a Spanish citizen can get a five-year residence permit. It is free and allows work anywhere in Spain.

other: Qualifying relationship with a Spanish national: spouse, registered or stable partner, children under 26 (or dependent), parents in your care, parent or guardian of a Spanish minor, and others in the Spaniard's care.
Stable partners generally need 12 months of cohabitation unless they have common children.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.

fees.label: Application fee
fees.note: The page says the procedure is free of charge.

routes.processing: Decision in 2 months. Silence is treated as a refusal.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Residence for relatives of Spanish nationals

routes.name: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens: free movement and registration
routes.summary: Citizens of EU and EEA countries and Switzerland can live in Spain under free-movement rules if they work, are self-employed, are a student or have enough resources and health insurance. Stays over three months need registration.

other: Must be employed, self-employed, a student with insurance and enough resources, or have enough resources and health coverage.
Registration certificate details (deadline, documents) are on the National Police portal, which we did not open.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 65, EU citizen registration certificate
Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 62, family member of an EU citizen

routes.name: Residence Card for Family of an EU Citizen
routes.summary: Non-EU relatives of an EU, EEA or Swiss citizen living in Spain apply for a family card valid five years. Covers spouses, registered partners, children under 21 or dependent, parents and some other dependents.

other: The EU citizen must be working, self-employed, a student with resources, or have enough resources and health insurance.
Apply within 3 months of entering Spain.

routes.processing: The card should be issued within 3 months of applying.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 62, family member of an EU citizen

routes.name: Social Arraigo (rooting) Residence
routes.summary: For people already in Spain without papers who have lived there continuously for at least two years. You need family ties or a positive social integration report. The permit lasts one year and allows work.

other: At least 2 years in Spain continuously before applying, with absences of no more than 90 days.
Either family ties (spouse, partner or first-degree relative with a residence permit, with combined means of 200% of IPREM) or a favorable social integration report from your region or city council.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.
Cannot be an international protection applicant, or hold another residence permit or have a pending one.

stay.note: The sheet says one year, each extension also one year, and extensions need proof of job searching. The official regulation press release says renewals after the first year are four years. Check which applies.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Social rooting sheet
Ministry of Inclusion: new Reglamento de Extranjería in force May 2025

routes.name: Socio-Labor Arraigo (rooting) Residence
routes.summary: For people living in Spain for at least two years who have a job contract of at least 20 hours a week paying at least the minimum wage. You can work for the employer while the application is processed.

other: At least 2 years of continuous residence in Spain before applying.
One or more contracts adding up to at least 20 hours a week and at least the minimum wage (or collective agreement wage), pro-rated.
Employer is up to date with taxes and Social Security.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years. Not an asylum applicant.

routes.processing: Decision within 3 months. Silence is treated as dismissed.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Socio-labor rooting sheet

routes.name: Socio-Training Arraigo (rooting) Residence
routes.summary: For people living in Spain for at least two years who are enrolling in qualifying training, such as vocational studies or a public employment service program. You also need a social integration report.

other: At least 2 years of continuous stay in Spain, absences up to 90 days.
Enrolled in or committed to qualifying training (post-compulsory secondary, vocational training, adult education, or a SEPE program for hard-to-fill jobs).
Social integration report from your region or city council.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.

routes.processing: The Aliens Office has 3 months to decide.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Socio-training rooting sheet

routes.name: Second Chance Arraigo (rooting) Residence
routes.summary: For people who held a residence permit within the last two years that was not renewed, and who have stayed in Spain continuously for two years. The permit lasts one year and allows work.

other: Held a prior residence permit (not an exceptional circumstances permit) within the two years before applying.
At least 2 years of continuous stay in Spain.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.
Cannot hold a residence permit or have a pending application.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Second chance rooting sheet

routes.name: Family Arraigo (rooting) Residence
routes.summary: For parents or guardians living with and caring for a minor child, or people supporting an adult with a disability, where the child or adult is an EU, EEA or Swiss national per the official page. No minimum time in Spain is required.

other: The official English page names EU, EEA or Swiss nationals. The Spanish regulation may be narrower or broader, so confirm the exact wording.
You must be in Spain, not an asylum applicant, and not hold another permit.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.

routes.processing: Decision within 3 months. Validity period was not stated on the page we could open.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Family rooting sheet

routes.name: Extraordinary Rooting (one-time 2026 regularization)
routes.summary: A one-time program for adults who were in Spain before January 1, 2026 and are still there. The application window opened in April 2026 (online April 16, in person April 20). The permit lasts one year and allows work. Check whether the window is still open.

other: In Spain before January 1, 2026 and still there, with at least 5 months of uninterrupted stay at application.
Plus one of: working or intending to work, employment contracts totaling more than 90 days in a year, living with a family unit, or being in a vulnerable situation certified by a social entity.
No criminal record, and not previously a holder of Ukrainian temporary protection.

routes.processing: Decision within 3 months. You can reside and work while the decision is pending.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 28 ter, extraordinary rooting

routes.name: Exceptional Circumstances Residence for Humanitarian Reasons
routes.summary: One-year residence permit that allows work for people in certain humanitarian situations, such as victims of some crimes, people with a serious illness that cannot be treated at home, or people in danger if they return.

other: Must fit a listed case: authorized stay under asylum or temporary protection rules, certain crime victims, serious illness needing care unavailable at home, or danger on return.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.

routes.processing: Decision within 3 months. Silence is treated as dismissed.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Humanitarian exceptional circumstances sheet

routes.name: Asylum and International Protection
routes.summary: You apply in person in Spain, ideally within one month of arriving, at the Oficina de Asilo y Refugio, a foreigners office, an authorized police station or an internment center. At the border you apply to the border police. The Interior Ministry decides.

other: You can remain in Spain while your application is being decided.
Free legal help and an interpreter are provided.
Permission to work if there is no final decision after 6 months.
You can appeal a negative decision to the Audiencia Nacional.

routes.processing: On Spanish territory you are told within 1 month whether the application is admitted. The authorities have up to 6 months to decide the case (3 months under the urgent procedure).

sources.label: Ministry of the Interior: Information for applicants for international protection (PDF)

routes.name: Long-Term Residence (national and EU long-term)
routes.summary: After five years of legal, continuous residence you can apply for long-term residence, which has no expiry. EU long-term residence adds an income requirement and the chance to move to other EU countries. Both allow you to live and work in Spain like a Spaniard.

other: Income rule: EU long-term residence: 150% of IPREM per month for a two-person family, plus 50% for each extra member. The page gives percentages only. IPREM is EUR 600 per month per another official page.
5 years of legal, continuous residence immediately before applying.
Absences up to 6 months each, no more than 10 months total in the 5 years (18 months if for work).
Study and training periods count at 50% for EU long-term residence.
No criminal record in Spain or countries lived in during the last 5 years.
Some other cases exist, such as contributory retirement or permanent incapacity pensions, and refugee status.

stay.note: No expiry. The identity card is renewed at age 5, then every 5 years until age 30, then every 10 years.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 49, national long-term residence
Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 50, EU long-term residence

routes.name: Permanent Residence Card for Family of an EU Citizen
routes.summary: Non-EU family members of an EU, EEA, Swiss or Spanish citizen can get a permanent card after five continuous years of legal residence as a family member. The card is valid ten years and renews automatically.

other: 5 continuous years of legal residence in Spain as a family member, with the family link kept.
Rights can also be kept after the citizen dies or after divorce in certain cases.

sources.label: Ministry of Inclusion: Sheet 63, permanent card for family of an EU citizen

routes.name: Citizenship by Residence (general, 10 years)
routes.summary: The general rule is 10 years of legal, continuous residence right before applying. Refugees need 5 years. You must show good conduct and pass the Instituto Cervantes tests, then swear loyalty and register.

eligibility.language: DELE Spanish diploma at level A2 or higher, for adults (exempt for nationals of listed Spanish-speaking countries)
other: Legal, continuous residence immediately before the application.
Pass the CCSE test on constitution and culture. A passed CCSE certificate is valid for 4 years.
Clean criminal record and civic conduct.
Oath to the King and the Constitution, and registration in the Civil Registry.

citizenship.note: You must renounce your previous nationality, except nationals of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal, and Sephardic people originally from Spain. Refugees need 5 years.

sources.label: Administracion.gob.es: Acquisition of nationality
BOE: Civil Code, articles 17 to 24
BOE: Orden JUS/1625/2016 (DELE and CCSE tests)

routes.name: Citizenship by Residence (2 years for Ibero-American and related nationals)
routes.summary: Nationals of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea and Portugal, and Sephardic people, need only 2 years of legal residence. They also do not have to give up their original nationality.

eligibility.language: DELE exemption for nationals of the Spanish-speaking countries listed in the 2016 order (for example Argentina, Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Chile, Venezuela, Dominican Republic)
other: 2 years of legal, continuous residence immediately before the application.
Pass the CCSE test. Oath to the King and the Constitution, and registration in the Civil Registry.
Clean criminal record and civic conduct.

citizenship.note: No renunciation of the original nationality is required for these nationalities.

sources.label: Administracion.gob.es: Acquisition of nationality
BOE: Civil Code, articles 17 to 24
BOE: Orden JUS/1625/2016 (DELE and CCSE tests)

routes.name: Citizenship by Marriage to a Spaniard (1 year)
routes.summary: If you have been legally resident and married to a Spaniard for at least one year (and not separated), you can apply for citizenship after just 1 year of residence. Widows and widowers of a Spaniard also qualify.

eligibility.language: DELE A2 or higher plus the CCSE test, unless exempt
other: Legal, continuous residence immediately before applying, with marriage to a Spaniard lasting at least 1 year and no legal or de facto separation.
Oath and registration in the Civil Registry. You must renounce your previous nationality unless exempt.

citizenship.note: Renunciation of the previous nationality is required unless you are from an exempt country (Ibero-American, Andorra, Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal).

sources.label: Administracion.gob.es: Acquisition of nationality
BOE: Civil Code, articles 17 to 24

routes.name: Citizenship by Descent (option and 1-year residence routes)
routes.summary: If your parent was originally Spanish and born in Spain, you can opt for Spanish nationality with no age limit. If your parent or grandparent was originally Spanish and you were born abroad, you can apply by residence after just 1 year in Spain. Spanish-by-origin parents pass nationality automatically.

other: Option route: father or mother originally Spanish and born in Spain (no age limit), or you are or were under the parental authority of a Spaniard (deadline age 20 unless extended).
1-year residence route: born abroad to a parent or grandparent who was originally Spanish.
Oath and registration in the Civil Registry. Renunciation of previous nationality is required unless exempt.
The special Democratic Memory Law (Law 20/2022) option window closed on October 22, 2025. Only people who requested an appointment before that deadline can still proceed.

citizenship.note: Born to a Spanish parent: Spanish by origin. Grandchild route is 1 year of residence in Spain.

sources.label: BOE: Civil Code, articles 17 to 24
Administracion.gob.es: Acquisition of nationality
Spain Consulate in Houston: End of the Democratic Memory Law window

routes.name: Citizenship by Birth
routes.summary: Spain does not give automatic citizenship to everyone born there. A child is Spanish by origin if one parent is Spanish, if one foreign parent was also born in Spain, or if the child would otherwise be stateless. Others born in Spain can apply by residence after 1 year.

other: Born to a Spanish parent, or to foreign parents where at least one was also born in Spain (diplomats excepted).
Born in Spain to stateless parents or parents whose laws give the child no nationality.
Others born in Spain can apply by residence after 1 year of legal residence.

citizenship.note: The 1-year residence route requires the usual oath, tests and registration. Renunciation rules apply unless exempt.

sources.label: BOE: Civil Code, articles 17 to 24
Administracion.gob.es: Acquisition of nationality

routes.name: Citizenship by Letter of Nature (exceptional grant)
routes.summary: A discretionary grant by Royal Decree for people with exceptional circumstances, such as cultural, sporting, scientific or charitable contributions. There is no standard route or timeline.

other: Exceptional circumstances must be shown. The decision is at the government's discretion.
Oath and registration in the Civil Registry.

sources.label: Administracion.gob.es: Acquisition of nationality
